seoTitle: Pitch Shifter: Change Key in Semitones, Same Tempo
metaDescription: Raise or lower the pitch of an audio file by semitones and cents without changing its length. Free online pitch shifter that runs in your browser.
intro: Shifts the pitch of an audio file up or down by semitones and cents while keeping the length the same, then saves a WAV file.
why:
Singers move a backing track into their range, players transpose a song for a capo or a different instrument, and producers fix a sample that is a little flat. The pitch has to change while the tempo stays put.

The tool time-stretches the clip by the opposite ratio with WSOLA, then resamples it so it plays back at the original length. This is a classic and simple method. It sounds good for shifts of a few semitones. Voices shifted by much more than four semitones start to sound unnatural because the formants move too.
howTo: Enter the semitones (positive is higher) and optional cents.
Listen to the result and download the WAV.

faq.q: How many semitones is a full tone?
faq.a: Two. A shift of 12 semitones is one octave.

faq.q: Why does the length stay the same?
faq.a: The tool stretches the audio by the inverse ratio first, then resamples, so the two changes cancel in length.

faq.q: Can it fix a slightly out-of-tune recording?
faq.a: For a whole-file offset, yes: use cents, for example +20. It cannot correct individual notes.
Yes. Both channels use the same alignment so the stereo image stays stable.
